intro: Hangeul is not pictures. It is 24 letters that spell sounds, arranged into square blocks — one block, one syllable. Most people can read it out loud within a week.

groups.title: The plain vowels
groups.blurb: A long line with a short mark on it. The short mark points at where the sound goes.

letters.hint: like the o in note, lips round
lips flat and wide, like the last sound in roses

groups.title: The y vowels
groups.blurb: Add a second short mark and a y slides in front of the sound.

letters.hint: ㅏ with a y in front
ㅓ with a y in front
ㅗ with a y in front
ㅜ with a y in front
also like the e in bed — modern Korean barely separates ㅐ and ㅔ
ㅐ with a y in front
ㅔ with a y in front

groups.title: The w vowels
groups.blurb: Two vowels written side by side. You say them as one slide.

groups.title: The plain consonants
groups.blurb: Each shape is a drawing of the mouth making the sound. ㄱ is the back of the tongue, ㄴ is the tip behind the teeth, ㅁ is the closed lips.

letters.hint: g at the start of a word, k at the end
d at the start, t at the end
between r and l — tongue taps once
b at the start, p at the end
s, but sh before ㅣ and ㅟ
silent at the front of a block, ng at the bottom

groups.title: The breathy consonants
groups.blurb: One extra stroke on the plain letter. That stroke is a puff of air — hold your hand in front of your mouth and you should feel it.

groups.title: The tight consonants
groups.blurb: The letter written twice. No puff of air at all — the throat squeezes and the sound comes out short and hard. This pair is what separates 자요 (sleeps) from 짜요 (salty).

blocks.title: How a block is built
rules: Every syllable starts with a consonant. If the sound starts with a vowel, ㅇ holds the empty seat: 아, 오, 이.
A tall vowel (ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ ㅐ) sits to the right: 가, 너, 미.
A wide vowel (ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅛ ㅠ) sits underneath: 고, 무, 스.
A closing consonant — the 받침 — goes at the bottom of the block: 밥, 문, 한.

blocks.title: The seven closing sounds
rules: Any letter can sit at the bottom of a block, but only seven sounds come out: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅁ, ㅂ, ㅇ.
ㅅ ㅆ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ ㅎ at the bottom are all said as a stopped ㄷ: 옷 is said ot, 꽃 is said kkot.
ㅋ ㄲ at the bottom are said as ㄱ. ㅍ at the bottom is said as ㅂ: 앞 is said ap.
When the next block starts with ㅇ, the closing sound slides across into it. 한국어 is said 한구거. This one rule makes spoken Korean sound nothing like it looks, and it is worth an hour of your time.
